topics.title: Introduction to Patterns
objectives: Student can identify repeating visual patterns in physical designs and daily life
Student can predict the next element in a simple repeating sequence of objects or shapes
visualIdeas: a sequence of repeating geometric shapes like triangle, square, circle with the next slot blank
a border design showing alternating colors and orientations of leaf shapes

topics.title: Patterns in Numbers
objectives: Student can identify arithmetic patterns in sequences of numbers
Student can calculate the missing terms in growing or shrinking number sequences
visualIdeas: a list of numbers 2, 4, 6, 8 with arrows showing addition of 2 at each step
a hundred grid table highlighting multiples of 5 to show diagonal patterns

topics.title: Rules from Patterns
objectives: Student can express a pattern rule using words
Student can determine the general rule of a sequence using variable placeholders like 'n'
visualIdeas: a table mapping step number to the number of matchsticks used to make a chain of triangles
a formula box highlighting the rule 'Number of matchsticks = 2n + 1'

topics.title: Visualizing Patterns
objectives: Student can draw geometric representations of square numbers and triangular numbers
Student can relate spatial arrangements of dots to numerical values
visualIdeas: dots arranged in triangles of size 1, 3, 6, 10 with equations underneath
a grid showing square numbers represented as L-shaped additions of dots

topics.title: Introduction to Geometry in Our Environment
objectives: Student can point out examples of lines, intersections, and angles in physical classroom surroundings
Student can describe how shapes are made of lines and vertices
visualIdeas: a sketch of a window frame with horizontal, vertical, and intersecting lines highlighted
a photo of a scissor showing different openings forming varying gap sizes

topics.title: Points, Lines, and Line Segments
objectives: Student can define the difference between a point, a line segment, and an infinite line
Student can label geometric lines and line segments using uppercase letter pairs with correct notation
visualIdeas: a comparison chart with a point, a line segment with two endpoints, and a line with double arrows
a ruler aligned with a line segment showing its definite measurable length

topics.title: Rays and Angles
objectives: Student can define a ray as starting from one point and extending infinitely in one direction
Student can label an angle formed by two rays sharing a common vertex
visualIdeas: a light beam emerging from a torch to illustrate a ray starting at a point
two rays sharing vertex O, with arrows pointing to the arms and vertex

topics.title: Measuring Angles
objectives: Student can line up a protractor baseline and center mark with an angle's vertex and arm
Student can read the degree measurement of a given angle on both scales of a protractor
visualIdeas: a step-by-step diagram of a protractor aligned to an angle showing the inner and outer scales
an angle of 60 degrees with the arc labeled with degree symbol

topics.title: Classification of Angles
objectives: Student can classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight, or reflex based on their degree measure
Student can draw angles belonging to each classification using a ruler and protractor
visualIdeas: a chart dividing angles into 5 types with representative drawings and their range inequalities
a rotating clock hand demonstrating acute, right, obtuse, straight, and reflex angle ranges

topics.title: Introduction to Play with Numbers
objectives: Student can define natural numbers and whole numbers
Student can arrange a set of multi-digit whole numbers in ascending and descending order
visualIdeas: a number line starting from zero to show whole numbers and highlighting natural numbers starting from one
a staircase visual where higher steps correspond to larger numbers

topics.title: Factors and Multiples
objectives: Student can list all the factors of any given number up to 100
Student can write down the first five multiples of a given single-digit number
visualIdeas: an array of 12 dots arranged in different rectangular layouts (1x12, 2x6, 3x4) to show factors
a number track showing skip jumping by 3s to represent multiples of 3

topics.title: Common Factors and Common Multiples
objectives: Student can identify common factors between two given numbers
Student can identify the first few common multiples of two given numbers
visualIdeas: a Venn diagram showing factors of 12 and 18 with their common factors in the overlap region
parallel number tracks for 4 and 6 with common multiples highlighted on both tracks

topics.title: Prime and Composite Numbers
objectives: Student can classify any given integer up to 100 as either prime or composite
Student can explain why 1 is neither prime nor composite
visualIdeas: a grid representation of the Sieve of Eratosthenes showing crossed-out composites and circled primes
a definition block highlighting the two-factor rule for primes versus multiple factors for composites

topics.title: Divisibility Rules
objectives: Student can test if a number is divisible by 2, 3, 5, 9, or 10 without performing complete division
Student can apply combination divisibility tests like divisibility by 6
visualIdeas: a flowchart outlining yes/no questions to test divisibility for 2, 3, 5, and 10
a color-coded breakdown of a number like 345 showing how the sum of digits 3+4+5=12 relates to divisibility by 3

topics.title: Introduction to Data
objectives: Student can explain what data is and identify examples of data collected in school and life
Student can recognize raw data versus organized data
visualIdeas: a random list of classroom favorite fruits compared side-by-side with a sorted list of the same fruits
a definition bubble explaining the terms 'Data', 'Information', and 'Observations'

topics.title: Collecting and Recording Data
objectives: Student can construct a tally marks table to organize raw observations into grouped counts
Student can read a tally frequency table to state which item occurs most or least frequently
visualIdeas: a dynamic step-by-step tally counter showing how four vertical lines are crossed by a fifth diagonal stroke
a complete tally table showing standard groupings of five for listing favorite sports of class students

topics.title: Pictographs
objectives: Student can interpret information represented by symbols in a pictograph
Student can construct a pictograph from a given table using an appropriate scale key
visualIdeas: a pictograph representing number of books with a book symbol equal to 5 books
a fraction of a symbol showing half the value of the standard key symbol

topics.title: Bar Graphs
objectives: Student can read a bar graph to determine quantities along the vertical and horizontal axes
Student can construct a bar graph with uniform width bars, correct labels, and equal spacing
visualIdeas: a labeled bar graph with colored vertical bars, horizontal grid lines, and a defined vertical axis scale
a checklist showing the essential elements of a bar graph: Title, Axes, Scale, and Uniform Spacing

topics.title: Introduction to Fractions and Factors
objectives: Student can link the concept of factors to division of objects
Student can identify a fraction as a part of a whole group or whole shape
visualIdeas: a whole square divided into equal parts, with some parts shaded to show the fraction concept
a collection of items grouped into subsets to illustrate part-of-a-collection fractions

topics.title: Prime Factorisation
objectives: Student can factorise any composite number into a product of prime numbers using a factor tree
Student can write down the prime factorisation of a number in power or product format
visualIdeas: a factor tree branching out from 36 down to its prime factors 2, 2, 3, 3
a division ladder displaying division by consecutive prime numbers to reach prime factorisation

topics.title: Highest Common Factor (HCF)
objectives: Student can calculate the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two or three numbers using prime factorisation
Student can solve simple daily life problems requiring the division of quantities into maximum equal portions
visualIdeas: parallel factorisations of two numbers with common factors highlighted and multiplied to find the HCF
a sketch of two containers of different capacities being measured exactly by a common third measuring can

topics.title: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
objectives: Student can calculate the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of two or three numbers using prime factorisation
Student can solve real-world problems involving simultaneous events occurring at regular intervals
visualIdeas: a table showing the step-by-step division method for finding the LCM of multiple numbers simultaneously
a timeline showing two bells ringing at intervals of 3 and 4 seconds, intersecting at 12 seconds

topics.title: Fractions and Fraction Types
objectives: Student can classify fractions into proper, improper, and mixed fractions
Student can convert an improper fraction to a mixed fraction and vice versa
visualIdeas: a chart showing a proper fraction with numerator less than denominator next to an improper fraction with the reverse
diagrams showing 5 halves equivalent to 2 whole blocks and 1 half block

topics.title: Fractions on the Number Line
objectives: Student can represent a given fraction as a point on a number line with equal subdivisions
Student can locate mixed numbers between correct consecutive whole numbers on the number line
visualIdeas: a portion of a number line between 0 and 1 divided into three equal segments to label 1/3 and 2/3
a zoom-in of a ruler between 2 and 3 showing the location of 2 and 1/2

topics.title: Equivalent Fractions
objectives: Student can construct equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same number
Student can simplify a given fraction to its lowest terms
visualIdeas: three circle fraction diagrams showing 1/2, 2/4, and 4/8 with equal shaded areas
equations showing the division of numerator and denominator by their HCF to simplify a fraction

topics.title: Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
objectives: Student can add and subtract fractions with like denominators
Student can calculate the sum and difference of unlike fractions using LCM to find common denominators
visualIdeas: a bar model showing 1/5 plus 2/5 resulting in a shaded area of 3/5
a step-by-step algebraic layout converting 1/2 and 1/3 to 3/6 and 2/6 before adding

topics.title: Multiplication of Fractions
objectives: Student can multiply a fraction by a whole number and interpret it as repeated addition
Student can multiply two fractions by multiplying numerators and denominators
visualIdeas: three individual blocks of size 1/4 joined together to equal 3/4
a grid representation where the overlap of vertical shading of 1/2 and horizontal shading of 2/3 shows their product

topics.title: Division of Fractions
objectives: Student can calculate the reciprocal of a fraction
Student can divide a fraction by another fraction or whole number by multiplying by the reciprocal
visualIdeas: a diagram illustrating how many halves are in 3 wholes using divided circle circles
a text box showing the conversion from 'divided by 3/4' to 'multiplied by 4/3'

topics.title: Introduction to Decimals
objectives: Student can explain tenths and hundredths as parts of a whole
Student can write down values represented on a place value table with decimal columns
visualIdeas: a grid of 10 blocks with 1 column colored to represent 0.1 or one-tenth
a place value chart containing Hundreds, Tens, Ones, tenths, hundredths, and thousandths with a vertical line marking the decimal point

topics.title: Decimals as Fractions and Vice Versa
objectives: Student can convert a decimal into a fraction in its simplest terms
Student can write any fraction with a denominator of 10, 100, or 1000 in decimal notation
visualIdeas: equations showing 0.25 written as 25/100, which then simplifies step-by-step to 1/4
a comparative scale aligning decimals 0.1, 0.2, 0.3... with fractions 1/10, 2/10, 3/10...

topics.title: Comparing Decimals
objectives: Student can compare two decimals to identify the greater one by looking at place values from left to right
Student can order a set of decimal numbers in ascending and descending order
visualIdeas: two decimal numbers 12.34 and 12.38 aligned vertically with the difference in the hundredths place highlighted
a list of decimal numbers ordered on a vertical staircase indicating increase in value

topics.title: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals
objectives: Student can align decimal numbers vertically with their decimal points in a single line before adding or subtracting
Student can solve word problems involving weights, lengths, or currency calculations with decimals
visualIdeas: a column addition problem showing placeholder zeros added to ensure equal decimal length alignment
a diagram of a shopping receipt where different item costs in Rupees and paise are aligned and totaled

topics.title: Introduction to Symmetry
objectives: Student can identify symmetric structures and patterns in nature, monuments, and artwork
Student can describe symmetry in their own words as a balanced proportion of halves
visualIdeas: a drawing of a butterfly and a leaf showing a split down the middle
a photo of the Taj Mahal showing the architectural balance on both sides of the central axis

topics.title: Line Symmetry
objectives: Student can test for line symmetry in shapes by folding them along an axis
Student can complete a partially drawn symmetric shape when the line of symmetry is given
visualIdeas: a paper folding illustration showing how one half of a heart shape matches the other perfectly
a grid worksheet with a dotted red line of symmetry and a half-drawn house shape to be mirrored

topics.title: Rotational Symmetry
objectives: Student can identify figures that look identical after rotation of less than 360 degrees
Student can state the order of rotational symmetry of common geometric shapes
visualIdeas: a windmill toy showing how rotating it by 90 degrees leaves its appearance unchanged
a step-by-step rotational sequence of an equilateral triangle showing matches at 120, 240, and 360 degrees

topics.title: Figures with Multiple Lines of Symmetry
objectives: Student can construct and count the multiple axes of symmetry in regular polygons
Student can compare shapes based on the number of lines of symmetry they possess
visualIdeas: an equilateral triangle with 3 lines of symmetry, a square with 4 lines, and a circle with infinite lines
a comparative table displaying polygons, their sides, and their corresponding number of symmetry axes

topics.title: Understanding Perimeter and Area
objectives: Student can distinguish between the boundary measurement (perimeter) and surface region (area) of shapes
Student can identify units used to measure perimeter versus area
visualIdeas: a diagram of a field with the fence highlighted in blue (perimeter) and the grass shaded in green (area)
a label box showing the comparison of 'cm' and 'm' for perimeter with 'sq.cm' and 'sq.m' for area

topics.title: Perimeter of Regular and Irregular Polygons
objectives: Student can calculate the perimeter of any polygon by summing all of its outer side lengths
Student can apply formulas to calculate the perimeter of squares, equilateral triangles, and rectangles
visualIdeas: an irregular pentagon with each of its five side lengths labeled and an addition equation underneath
a formula breakdown graphic showing 'Perimeter of a Rectangle = 2 x (Length + Breadth)' with dimensions

topics.title: Area by Grid Counting
objectives: Student can estimate the area of any closed shape drawn on a squared grid paper by counting full, half, and more-than-half squares
Student can state why grid squares are standard units of area measurement
visualIdeas: a leaf silhouette placed over a square grid with counted squares marked with checkmarks and fractions
a standard square of size 1 cm by 1 cm labeled as 1 square centimeter

topics.title: Area of Rectangles and Squares
objectives: Student can derive the area formula of a rectangle by grid arrangement of unit squares
Student can calculate the area of squares and rectangles given their side dimensions
visualIdeas: a rectangle of length 5 cm and width 3 cm filled with 15 individual 1-sq-cm grid tiles
formula text boxes for Area of Rectangle (l x b) and Area of Square (side x side) with worked numerical examples

topics.title: Introduction to Algebra
objectives: Student can differentiate between arithmetic expressions using numbers and algebraic statements using variables
Student can identify the unknown parts in a mathematical relation
visualIdeas: a balance scale comparing a known weight side (5 + 3) to a side with a mystery bag (x + 2)
a slide contrasting arithmetic equations with algebraic expressions containing letters

topics.title: The Concept of Variables
objectives: Student can describe a variable as a symbol or letter that can stand for any number in a set
Student can use variables to state simple mathematical rules like geometry perimeter formulas
visualIdeas: a sequence of matchstick squares with a rule box showing variables representing variable counts
a character explaining that letter symbols represent changing numerical values

topics.title: Expressions with Variables
objectives: Student can translate verbal statements into algebraic expressions
Student can construct numerical values of an expression by substituting given numbers for variables
visualIdeas: a matching game layout with verbal cards like '5 more than x' connecting to expression cards like 'x + 5'
a step-by-step substitution flow showing 'Evaluate 3y + 4 for y = 2' leading to '3(2) + 4 = 10'

topics.title: Concept of an Equation
objectives: Student can explain an equation as a condition on a variable where two sides are equal
Student can solve simple equations using the trial-and-error inspection method
visualIdeas: a balanced scale where left pan 'x + 3' balances right pan '7', showing x must be equal to 4
a trial-and-error value table testing different values of x to see which one makes the equation LHS equal RHS
